sentences.text: The appellant is in judicial custody.
The appellant has filed a bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail before the Special Court, which came to be dismissed.
Therefore, the appellant is before this Court.

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is innocent and as per the statements and the order passed by the trial Court, the appellant was not present in the house at the time of incident.
He further submitted that in the death note also the name of the appellant is not forthcoming and it is categorically stated in the death note that the appellant is not responsible.
He submitted that the appellant is in custody for more than 8 months, investigation is completed and charges sheet is also filed and the other accused persons were already on bail.
Hence he prays that on these grounds, the appellant is entitled for bail.

6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader objected for grant of bail and contended that the accused was also inside the house and he did not allow the deceased to enter the house and made her to sit from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., therefore, she has committed suicide.

In the death note the deceased also stated that at the instance of the other accused, the appellant used to harass the deceased physically demanding more dowry and taking her caste name which NC: 2023:KHC:20772 provoked the deceased to commit suicide within seven years of their marriage, which attracts Section 498A and 304B of IPC.
Hence, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

7. Having heard learned Counsel for the appellant and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State and having perused the material on record, it is seen from the records that the marriage of the appellant and the deceased Lakshmi was held after panchayath was convened by elders of both sides and out of their wedlock, a female child was born aged about 3 years.
It is seen from the complaint that there were frequent quarrels between them by assaulting the deceased and demanding dowry.
There were many panchayats held during the lifetime of the deceased.
It is also seen from the complaint that the complainant took the deceased along with her grand daughter to Nagaraja Reddy vs The State Of Karnataka

3 their house for three days and thereafter giving advise to the deceased Lakshmi, they went to the house of the accused along with his co-sister Rukkamma.
When they reached the house of the accused, the other accused did not allow them to enter the house but the accused was not present in the house.
Hence, they went to the work NC: 2023:KHC:20772 place of the appellant where the appellant picked up quarrel with them and took his motorbike and went away.
When she along with her co-sister Rukkamma came back to the house of the accused, the other accused did not allow them to enter the house.
Later Rukkamma went back to her house.
At about 3.00 p.m. the complainant went to a hotel to bring lunch for the deceased Lakshmi and when she returned at about 4.30 p.m. she saw that Lakshmi committed suicide by hanging herself.
Since the accused did not allow the deceased inside the house, the deceased committed suicide.
Immediately the deceased was shifted to hospital but declared dead.

Further the statement of the CW.1 and CW.6 clearly reveal that there was continuous harassment on the deceased by the appellant even on the date of her death even though there were many panchayaths held.
The appellant being the husband of the deceased Lakshmi harassed the deceased which abetted her to commit suicide.

The death note reveals that on the advise of the family members, the appellant used to come to the house in a drunken stage and assaulted the deceased physically, which also abetted the deceased to commit suicide.

Even after the marriage the appellant was harassing the deceased by NC: 2023:KHC:20772 taking her caste name, which also attracts Section 3(1)(r), (1)(s) and 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Act and also harassing the deceased by demanding dowry which attracts Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Merely the appellant is in judicial custody.
There is no ground to allow the appeal and grant bail to the appellant as he has committed serious offences.
If he is released on bail, there is likelihood of the appellant tampering the prosecution witness and absconding from the case is not ruled out and it will give a wrong message to the society.
Therefore, the trial Court has rightly rejected the petition and bail application.
Hence, it does not call for interference.
The appeal is dismissed.
